data.note:
Reflection: Conclusion Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.92) correctly matches BBBC021 annotation for AZ258. Compound identity not in PubChem/ChEMBL per unblinding note; no curated ChEMBL mechanism to verify, but phenotypic evidence convergent:

- Morphometric: frac_large_nucleus z=70-101, nuc_area z=38-45, nuc_major_axis z=23-30, nuc_dna_integrated z=8-15, reduced solidity/form_factor, increased cell_area/major_axis across 0.3-3 µM (e2,e4,e5,e10,e11), with no tubulin loss/bundling (tub_mean z ~ -1.6 to 2.2, e14) and no mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like z negative, e12) - distinguishes from microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors which increase mitotic fraction.
- Visual: microscopist confirmed enlarged 1.5-2x nuclei, lobulated/bilobed irregular contours, increased integrated DNA/polyploidy, spread enlarged cells with preserved tubulin/actin network (e6,e7 low uncertainty).
- Atlas: 9/10 neighbors Aurora inhibitors (AZ841, AZ-A) similarity 0.90-0.97 vs 0.83 for DNA damage (e8); high-dose 30 µM profile shifted to lower similarity microtubule stabilizer-like (e9) consistent with off-target cytotoxicity but core doses unequivocal.
- Dose-response: plateaued large-nucleus phenotype then decline at 30 µM with cell loss (e13) consistent with Aurora B cytokinesis failure leading to polyploidy then toxicity.

Literature support: TNK2 inhibitor causing polyploidization through mitotic failure by targeting Aurora B illustrates the polyploid/large-nucleus mechanism (PMID:39639371); Aurora A inhibition modulating mitotic delay vs microtubule agents supports discrimination from microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers (PMID:19221504); PP1-Aurora B balance for chromosome segregation/cytokinesis underpins lobulated multinucleation phenotype (PMID:18716057). Follow-up proposed pHH3 Ser10 + DNA flow distinguishes Aurora from DNA damage/replication was appropriate.

No errors; high confidence justified.

reflection.text:
Reflection - AZ258 unblinded as Aurora kinase inhibitors - Verdict: CORRECT (p=0.92)

What the evidence got right:
- The primary phenotype was captured by repeated morphometric hits across the active window, not a single well: w_8b561f0561 (0.3 uM, 421 cells) frac_large_nucleus z=+80.7, w_7d742a2ea2 (1 uM, 350 cells) z=+70.3, w_c427c37b1c (3 uM, 265 cells) z=+101.4, with concordant nuc_area z=+38-44.9 and nuc_major_axis z=+22.7-29.6. This is the classic polyploid/enlarged nucleus signal. describe_phenotype e6 and e7 both independently called lobulated/bilobed large nuclei and listed Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (e6: 7 observations density lower, e7: 7 observations density similar), providing visual confirmation against a fragmented DNA damage look.
- compare_to_reference_atlas e8 was decisive: 9/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors at similarity 0.90-0.97 vs 1/10 DNA damage at 0.83. This allowed correct down-weighting of DNA replication (0.03) and DNA damage (0.02) despite e7 listing DNA replication as secondary candidate and e8 containing one DNA damage neighbour. The separation in similarity scores was properly used.
- Negative controls for mitotic arrest were correct: dose_response of frac_mitotic_like over 4 wells rho=+0.00 p=1 (e12) - down not up - arguing against Eg5 inhibitors / microtubule destabilizers which trap mitosis. This is consistent with literature that Aurora inhibition abrogates mitotic delay induced by microtubule perturbing agents PMID 19221504, and that Aurora B is required for chromosome segregation and cytokinesis PMID 18716057. The polyploidization through mitotic/cytokinesis failure mechanism described in PMID 39639371 directly supports the enlarged, lobulated nuclei + low mitotic fraction interpretation used in update_hypotheses 0.92.
- Tubulin intact at active doses: e2,e4,e5 showed no tub disruption at 0.3-3 uM, and dose_response tub_mean rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e14) correctly argued against microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer as primary MoA at relevant concentrations.

What misled / what was missed and why:
- Acquisition of the highest dose w_bb49de52e8 (30 uM e3) was the main distractor: tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.9, act_glcm_contrast z=+22.6, tub_std z=+15.9, and compare_to_reference_atlas e9 returned Microtubule stabilizers 8/10. Taken alone this would have supported 0.01 hypothesis for Microtubule stabilizers. It was correctly flagged in update_hypotheses as contradicting e2,e4,e5,e6,e14 because the large-nucleus phenotype was lost at 30 uM and cell count was lower (165 cells vs 265-421), indicating isolated high-dose/cytotoxic tubulin texture change, not the 0.3-3 uM MoA. The review correctly approved on this basis.
- dose_response statistics were underpowered and non-significant by design: e10 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e11 nuc_area rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e13 cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 across only 4 wells (single rep per dose 0.3-30 uM per list_available_experiments constraint of 4 wells). We initially included e10,e11 as supporting in hypothesis_history but they do not show monotonic trend - they only show consistency/flat high signal across 0.3-3 uM with drop at 30 uM. This was handled by not over-interpreting p-values and relying on absolute z-scores and atlas instead.
- lookup_compound errors contributed no mechanistic value: AZ258 returned no curated mechanisms (expected for BBBC021 blind), AZ841 failed lookup entirely, and epothilone B lookup confirmed Tubulin stabiliser by name only. This meant chemical prior could not be used - ranking had to rely entirely on phenotype/atlas, which was appropriate but leaves p=0.92 not 0.99.
- Density discrepancy between e6 (lower) and e7 (similar) vs DMSO was not resolved but did not affect call; cell_count dose_response non-significant was consistent with cytostatic polyploidy rather than acute cytotoxicity at active doses.

Acquisition choices: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM with only 4 wells affordable. Sampling 0.3,1,3,30 uM was discriminative - it captured onset, plateau, and high-dose toxicity in one sweep. Trade-off was single replicate per dose, which produced large per-well n (165-421 cells) but weak Spearman stats. A better split would have been 2 replicates at 0.3 and 1 uM to strengthen mitotic and tubulin negatives, but ranking would not have changed given e8 9/10 Aurora dominance.

No clinical implications are inferred; proposed pHH3 Ser10 + DNA content follow-up remains a research validation assay only.

Acquisition choices: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM with only 4 wells affordable. Sampling 0.3,1,3,30 uM was discriminative - it captured onset, plateau, and high-dose toxicity in one sweep. Trade-off was single replicate per dose, which produced large per-well n (165-421 cells) but weak Spearman stats. A better split would have been 2 replicates at 0.3 and 1 uM to strengthen mitotic and tubulin negatives, but ranking would not have changed given e8 9/10 Aurora dominance.

No clinical implications are inferred; proposed pHH3 Ser10 + DNA content follow-up remains a research validation assay only.

What was right:
- e2 e4 e5 repeated frac_large_nucleus z 70-101 and nuc_area z 38-44.9 across 0.3-3uM with 265-421 cells each correctly identified polyploidy
- e6 e7 visual lobulated/bilobed nuclei both listed Aurora kinase inhibitors
- e8 atlas 9/10 Aurora 0.90-0.97 vs DNA damage 1/10 0.83 correctly separated Aurora 0.92 from DNA replication 0.03 DNA damage 0.02
- e12 frac_mitotic_like rho 0.00 down not up correctly excluded Eg5/microtubule arrest, e14 tub_mean intact at active doses

What was wrong or missed:
- e3 e9 30uM tub_glcm_contrast +28.9 act_glcm_contrast +22.6 atlas 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers misleading if taken as primary MeA
- e10 e11 e13 dose_response rho -0.40 p0.6 underpowered across 4 wells misreadable as lack of dose effect rather than plateau plus high-dose loss
- lookup_compound no curated mechanisms for AZ258 and failed AZ841 lookup provided no orthogonal confirmation

Proposed next experiment: Phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence + DNA content flow cytometry across 0.03-3µM to validate Aurora-specific loss of pHH3 and >4N polyploid peak vs DNA damage controls - research use only, not clinical.
